Motto, Vision & Expectations
At Southborough, we support every child to flourish in an ever changing world, through a nurturing and inclusive environment.
We deliver a rich curriculum where children develop life long memories and a passion for learning.
Together with families, staff and the wider community we build a foundation where children are kind, independent, resilient and responsible.

Galaxy – Before & After-School Club
Welcome to Galaxy. We hope the following information will be of help to new Parents/Carers.
The aim of the Galaxy club is to provide parents with affordable quality child care during term time.
We have a dedicated and caring team of play workers who plan activities with the help of the children. There are plenty of games and equipment, including computers for the children’s use.
Parents are not allowed to drive onto site (including the BYMT). Please park in Oxhawth Crescent and use the side gate to the school. Follow the path until you arrive at the conservatory. Ring the bell and a member of staff will meet you at the door.
The children are signed in on the register at every session. Children attending after school sessions will be signed out by club manager or a staff member.
Parents must advise the manager if the child is going to be absent or if the child is not being collected by the nominated parent/carer.
Breakfast and afternoon snacks are provided for your child/children, so we would ask that you do not send extra snacks in to the club. Sweets or products containing nuts are not allowed in the club.
Morning sessions are: 7.45am – 8.55am
On arrival the children are signed in on the register and hang their coats up before choosing their breakfast. At present the breakfast menu at present is as follows: cereals, toast or crumpets and various spreads, fresh fruit, raisins, milk, fruit juice, water, and in cold weather hot chocolate.
At 8.45am KS2 children are escorted to their classrooms by Galaxy staff
Reception and KS1 children are escorted to their class rooms at 8.45am again by Galaxy staff.
Afternoon sessions are: 3.15pm – 6pm.
Reception and year 1 children are brought to Galaxy by the school staff and KS2 children make their own way to the club. They are signed in on the register before having a snack.
The afternoon snack menu is on a 3 week rota which is available for your information on the school website.
When the children are collected the club manager or staff will sign them out from the register.
Our telephone number is 020 8467 2343 Press 5 to speak to the Galaxy club in session time or to leave a message on the answer phone.
All Galaxy place admissions must come via website form or school provided Galaxy form as emails will not be counted as place requests.
Galaxy spaces are permanent, continuous allocated spaces until a parent/carer states that the space is no longer needed and a 2 week notice period then comes into effect.
Places are awards as follows:
Ad-hoc sessions can be provided to already attending Galaxy children if space is available on days needed at an extra cost for emergencies but not a service regularly offered
New September school starters are not automatically assigned a Galaxy place and must apply via the website form or school provided starter pack.
Should you have any concerns please do not hesitate to speak to Sonia.
We hope you and your children enjoy your time at Galaxy.
Sonia Ahmet (Manager)

Curriculum
Curriculum Rationale
The curriculum in TPA schools is designed to inspire and motivate children. Our aim is for every child to experience ‘an extraordinary school day’ every day. We place children at the heart of the learning process through a bespoke ‘Teaching and Learning Model.’ The Model, which is rooted firmly in research and analysis of effective learning and teaching, translates the Trust’s Expectations into classroom practice. This Model has been developed and embedded to provide consistency and continuity for all children.
The Curriculum for Unity School’s Partnership (CUSP) is used for Reading, Writing, Spelling, Science, History, Geography, Art and DT. This is an ambitious, evidence-based curriculum with a focus on vocabulary. It is a coherent subject-specific, knowledge-based curriculum has been developed with carefully planned sequences of learning that reflect the National Curriculum. End points are identified and carefully planned for, building on previous knowledge. Long term plans comprehensively map out what is taught across the school in all subjects. Subjects are taught individually in half termly units, but links are made across different subjects where appropriate.
The Pioneer Academy is committed to the highest quality teaching across the whole curriculum and promotes the use of specialist teachers to facilitate this. We currently have specialist teachers across our schools, such as PE, Art, Music, Computing and MfL.
The White Rose Mathematics scheme, supplemented by additional resources, is used for teaching and learning in Mathematics. This was selected for its accessibility and strong approach to mastery.
CUSP (Curriculum with Unity Schools Partnership) is the curriculum used for reading, writing and spelling (KS2 only). It is also used for Science, History, Geography, Art and DT. It was chosen for its coherent curriculum design and instructional teaching. It is underpinned by explicit vocabulary instruction and research-focused pedagogy.
Little Wandle Phonics is used across the trust and has been selected for the level of structure and resourcing available.
In EYFS a thematic approach is used and this is being developed to lay the foundations for the curriculum, knowledge and skills taught in Year 1 and beyond.
Our teaching and learning model is designed and implemented in such a way that it builds on prior knowledge and skills and lays the foundation for future learning. Lessons are designed to be engaging and challenging with learners actively involved.
Long-term plans have been created so that subject coverage is planned sequentially and with a clear rationale for making connections with prior learning, therefore learning is blended and refined. Our curriculum planning is supplemented by a wide range of opportunities and enrichment activities which allow for cross curricular learning. This enables learners to see the ‘Big Picture’ of their learning and to make connections both through and across different subjects.
We review the impact of our curriculum continuously in a variety of different ways. We monitor how effectively our curriculum and enrichment provision provides opportunities for each unique pupil to reach their full potential.
We look at the quality and breadth of work seen in learner’s books, online and in the learning environment, pupil voice discussions, outcomes of assessments and quality of teaching and learning through learning walks. All of these tools help us assess the consistency, impact and relevance of our curriculum.
Monitoring and Evaluation
Regional Directors and central team members monitor whether the school is complying with TPA teaching and learning expectations through:
Learning Walks with members of the Senior Leadership Team and the school’s wider leadership team.
Meetings with subject leaders to support and challenge them.
Evaluation meetings such as Stakeholder Visits to hold senior leaders to account
Senior Leaders and Subject Leaders monitor the way the curriculum is taught throughout the school in the following ways:
Book looks (Coverage/Breadth/Progression)
Work scrutinies (Quality of work)
Learning environment walks
Pupil voice surveys and interviews
Learning walks followed by developmental coaching
Analysing teacher assessment of their subject across the school
At TPA, learning is at the heart of all we do and so assessment is used to shape future learning. It is not excessive or onerous and forms part of the day to day working practices of the classroom. Teachers ensure that pupils embed key concepts in their long-term memory. Key skills and objectives for curriculum areas are revisited throughout the year and applied in different contexts. We also use summative assessments to support the teacher's overall assessment in these subjects.
Children take part in quizzes to support the recall of facts and information. A wide range of strategies such as questioning, talk partner discussions, using mini whiteboards and a range of other teaching strategies are also used to assess knowledge.

FRIENDS OF SOUTHBOROUGH
Address: Southborough Primary School, Southborough Lane, Bromley, Kent BR2 8AA Telephone: 020 8467 2343 Charity Number: 297867 Web: www.fospta.co.uk Email: friendsofsouthborough@hotmail.com
Friends of Southborough
Did you know that now your child is at Southborough Primary School you automatically become a member of Friends of Southborough (FoS)? FoS is important to the school. It is set up as a charity so that all monies raised are tax-free for the school to use. It is a very important asset for the school and we are currently looking for new recruits.
How about volunteering to join the Committee and helping to raise extra funds for the school? As well as raising money, which is always needed, we try to make the events fun and varied for the children and their families. It adds to the community feel of the school if everyone can get involved and it’s a great way to meet other families.
There are currently about a dozen active members on the Committee and lots of volunteers prepared to give up time to help at events.
Joining the Committee is a fantastic way to meet new people and become more involved with the school. Generally the Committee meets every 4-6 weeks but again that depends on forthcoming events and what needs to be talked about.
For more information email friendsofsouthborough@hotmail.com or ask the school office to introduce you to a Committee member.
